clue.text: Picture pain mainly under Dr Flower

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under another follows it

parts.note: a snap is a photograph, a picture
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, taken as written

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: agony is great pain

explanation.surface: Someone in pain consults a doctor about a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims AGONY to AGON, which goes under DR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden plant grown for its colourful blooms.

clue.text: Large seabird is duck's victim

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O, with the 's kept
prey is another word for a victim, something hunted

explanation.surface: A big seabird hunts a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so it gives O; the 's stays as S.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a large fish-eating bird of prey found by coasts.

clue.text: Island once shown by name? It is back in maps

indicators.note: in tells us the name and the turned word sit inside the maps

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: back means the word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: A question whether a lost island is shown in a book of maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT to TI; N and TI go inside ATLAS, after its second A.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island said to have sunk beneath the sea long ago.

clue.text: Chap backing mature store selling wine

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person, a chap

indicators.note: backing here means the following word is turned round

parts.note: to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A man backs a mature business selling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AGE to EGA, which follows BOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar, so a store selling wine.

clue.text: Most peculiar individual runs, wearing fancy tweeds

indicators.note: wearing means the anagrammed tweeds go round the other letters like clothes
fancy signals the letters of tweeds are rearranged

parts.note: I is a single one, an individual
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An eccentric loner goes running in fancy tweeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns TWEEDS into WEDEST; 'wearing' puts I and R inside, after WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weirdest is the superlative of weird, meaning strangest or oddest.

clue.text: Game of pool?

parts.note: read as a sport played in a swimming pool, the water version of a horseback game; its letters also rearrange those of pool

explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is played in a pool, so the game named here is the one of the pool.

clue.text: Attitude required to look after group

parts.note: to mind is to look after, as in minding children
a set is a group

explanation.surface: The right attitude is needed to care for a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a settled way of thinking, an attitude.

clue.text: Speaking about refreshing drink being appetising

indicators.note: about means the word for speaking goes around the drink

parts.note: mouthing is saying words, speaking
water is a refreshing drink

explanation.surface: Talking about a refreshing drink makes it sound tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: WATER sits inside MOUTHING, after MOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth-watering food is tempting, so it describes something appetising.

clue.text: Taxing individual with sour disposition

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement signals the letters of sour are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demanding person with a sour temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but means arrangement: SOUR becomes ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome, so it is taxing.

clue.text: Foolishly greets waspish asides from an actor

indicators.note: foolishly signals the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly meets snide remarks from a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges GREETS and WASPISH together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage whispers are loud asides delivered by an actor for the audience to hear.

clue.text: Paper's cue for circulation in capital

indicators.note: circulation suggests the letters are sent round into a new order

parts.note: the word paper with its s kept

explanation.surface: A newspaper's prompt for its circulation figures in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' looks like newspaper sales but rearranges PAPERS and CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are also called upper-case letters.

clue.text: Sources of rum in Oman? Just any wine!

indicators.note: sources of means we take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Asking whether in Oman any old wine will do instead of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of rum, in, Oman, Just, any spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of Spain.

clue.text: Oliver Thomas is tough

definitions.meaning: two famous bearers of one surname: Oliver of Laurel and the comedy duo, and Thomas the Wessex novelist
robust and able to endure harsh conditions

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver and Thomas both share the surname, and the word also means robust or tough.

clue.text: List covering ethnicity can be found

indicators.note: covering means the list goes around the other word

parts.note: a table is a list of figures
race is a word for ethnicity

explanation.surface: A list that records ethnicity can be tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: RACE goes inside TABLE, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traceable can be tracked down, so it can be found.

clue.text: Man getting in touch with his feminine side in church?

definitions.text: Man getting in touch with his feminine side in church?

parts.words: Man getting in touch with his feminine side in church?
parts.note: not a man exploring his gentle nature but one physically beside a woman at the altar, at his wedding

explanation.definitionFit: At a church wedding the man standing at the side of his bride is the newly married husband.

clue.text: The Spanish invested in Scotsman's service

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as in clothing someone

parts.note: Angus is a typically Scottish man's name
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Spanish people put money into a Scottish man's business.
explanation.walkthrough: EL goes inside ANGUS, after ANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion recited at set times, a form of service.

clue.text: Love to leave work on miners' plant

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
to leave says the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: labour is work
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

explanation.surface: A request that love abandon work for a plant belonging to miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes O out of LABOUR, giving LABUR, which sits on NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Laburnum is a small tree with drooping yellow flowers, so a plant.

clue.text: Sort of pet shark or other aquatic creature

parts.note: a cat is one kind of pet
a shark is one kind of fish, and so are many others

explanation.surface: A pet, a shark, or some other water creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The catfish is a whiskered fish living in water, an aquatic creature.

clue.text: Softly supporting company in a convincing way

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: gently means softly

explanation.surface: Speaking softly while backing a company, and persuasively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts GENTLY below CO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguing cogently means arguing clearly and persuasively.

clue.text: Honouring none dressed with flashy jewellery

indicators.note: dressed as in prepared or arranged signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone honours nobody wearing showy jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges NONE to ENNO, followed by BLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennobling someone raises them to the nobility, so it is honouring them.

clue.text: Makes slow progress at home, not finishing game

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Someone at home plods through a game they never finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' trims CHESS to CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move very slowly, so inches means makes slow progress.

clue.text: Reckon people invited have no time

indicators.note: have no means the letter is removed

parts.note: guests are people invited

explanation.surface: Thinking the invited people have no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no' takes T out of GUESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to estimate, which is what reckon means.

clue.text: Foreigner's broad smile on exit

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
to go is to exit

explanation.surface: A foreigner grins as they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Foreigner's is read as 'is' linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gringo is a slang term in Latin America for a foreigner, especially an English speaker.

clue.text: Subject oneself to a hot dog?

parts.note: hot meaning fashionable is in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A question of whether to put up with a hot dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dog' looks like a sausage, but hot gives IN and dog gives CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur something is to bring it upon oneself.

clue.text: The expense of beginning to sleep in bed

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letter goes inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: How much it costs to start sleeping in a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside COT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cost is the price paid, the expense of something.

clue.text: Caretaker's cold, working EEC rig at sea

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A caretaker has a cold while working on an oil rig at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Caretaker's is read as 'is'. 'at sea' rearranges EEC RIG into CIERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge looks after a building and its residents, a caretaker.

clue.text: Handy expression for joke you're listening to

indicators.note: listening to means the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: jest is a joke, so this is jest you're

explanation.surface: A joke told to someone listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jest you're' said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement of the hand used to express something.

clue.text: A thug hired in case of leaks in such sea areas

indicators.note: in places the thug inside the outer letters
case of means the outside letters of the word, like a case around it

parts.note: a goon is a thug

explanation.surface: A thug is paid to deal with leaks in sea areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' leaks gives L and S; A GOON goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagoons are stretches of shallow sea water cut off by reefs or sandbanks.
